declarations.description: A before/after slider: two layers on top of each other, the after layer cut at a divider the reader drags, as in a retouched photo, a redesign or two map layers. The `before` and `after` slots take any element: an ``, a `c2-image`, a ``, a map. The before layer sets the size; the after layer is laid over it and clipped to the divider, so the reader sees the before layer on the left (on top with `orientation="vertical"`) and the after layer past the divider. `position` is the share of the before layer shown, from 0 to 100 (default 50). Drag the handle, or press anywhere on the images, to move the divider; with `hover`, it follows the pointer without a press. `before-label` and `after-label` draw chips in the corners; each belongs to its layer, so the divider cuts it as it passes over. `input` fires while the divider moves and `change` once it settles (on release, or after a key); read `position`. The handle is a `slider`. Its name is `label`, else "Compare: …" built from the layers' alternative text. The arrow keys move it 1% in the direction pressed, Page Up and Page Down 10%, Home and End to the edges.

slots.description: The layer shown before the divider: on the left, or on top when vertical. It sets the component's size.

slots.description: Replaces the grip drawn in the handle.

members.name: label

members.name: hoverMoved
members.description: Set while `hover` moved the divider since the pointer came in, so leaving fires one `change`.

members.name: moveTo
members.description: Sets the position and fires `input` (and `change` when it settles at once), unless it did not move.

members.name: positionAt
members.description: The position under the pointer, measured only while the reader moves it.

members.name: nameOf
members.description: The alternative text of a slotted layer: an image's `alt`, else its `aria-label`, else a nested image's `alt`.

events.description: When the divider settles: on release, or after a key.

events.name: input
events.description: While the divider moves, by pointer or key. Read `position`.
